goldens.comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
goldens.reasoning: G1 is about removing the float-based right alignment of the .d-header .panel. C4 does say floats are ignored on flex items, but it is about the .small-action button. That is a different element and a different layout problem.

goldens.comment: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
goldens.reasoning: C1 flags the same invalid -ms-align-items property and gives the same fix, -ms-flex-align.

goldens.comment: -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.
goldens.reasoning: C2 makes the same point that box-ordinal-group starts at 1, so passing the order value unchanged causes mis-ordering.

candidates: -ms-align-items is not a valid IE10/11 flexbox property (the correct one is -ms-flex-align), keeping the invalid property can trip CSS linters and adds noise

@mixin order sets -webkit-box-ordinal-group/-moz-box-ordinal-group to the same value as the modern order, but in the legacy flexbox spec box-ordinal-group is 1-based (default 1), so it should be order + 1; otherwise items will be mis-ordered in browsers that still honor the prefixed properties
align-items:$alignment is missing the usual spacing

.small-action is now a flex container, but .small-action-desc doesn't flex to fill remaining space. Since float is ignored on flex items, the trailing button will no longer be pushed to the right unless the description grows (or the button is auto-margined)
